investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T14:57–15:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 126–148 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The four remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling. Because no VM is ever provisioned, the eval probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling phase, and the check terminates with an Unschedulable error rather than returning any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new pods.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource entirely (not registered or not labeled), so they are excluded by both the resource request and the pod's node affinity/selector, making the capacity problem structurally worse than a simple quota issue.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node drain, or node failure reduced the number of kata-peerpods-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking available vm-slot capacity below the level needed to schedule eval probes concurrently with production workloads.

[Possible] The pod's node affinity/selector is overly restrictive (e.g., targeting a specific node pool label) and no longer matches the nodes that have remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, creating a mismatch even if raw capacity exists elsewhere in the cluster.

[Less likely] A misconfiguration in the remote-agent pod spec (resource request quantity for kata.peerpods.io/vm) was recently changed to a value that exceeds per-node limits, making the pod unschedulable even on otherwise eligible nodes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the scheduler message would need a different explanation (e.g., a bug in the resource accounting plugin).

If re-running the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held lock or a race condition during concurrent probe runs) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the affinity/selector is confirmed correct, the problem is isolated to the 2 eligible nodes only and the affinity hypothesis is disproved.

If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, the resource exhaustion hypothesis is disproved and the cause may be a node-level plugin failure or misconfigured resource advertisement.

If the pod spec's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request quantity was recently changed to exceed per-node limits, that would shift the cause from capacity exhaustion to a misconfigured request, which would be disproved if the request quantity matches historical values.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all cluster nodes and warns when available slots fall below a configurable threshold (e.g., fewer than N slots remaining), providing early warning before pod scheduling fails.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum count, alerting when the eligible node pool shrinks to a level that risks scheduling failures under concurrent load.

Add a dedicated eval for the kata-peerpods node plugin health that confirms the extended resource is correctly advertised on all expected nodes, catching plugin failures or mis-labeling before they cause scheduling outages.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes between 'pod scheduled but VM not ready' and 'pod never scheduled', enabling faster triage of scheduling vs. VM-provisioning failures in future incidents.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T15:00–15:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the runner never reached the state-polling step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. Every attempt to schedule a new remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because no pod could be scheduled, createAgent() in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never returned a live agent, and the state-polling logic that would produce orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence was never reached. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in all three check messages.

Preemption policy prevents eviction of lower-priority pods: the scheduler found no preemption victims on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning existing pods are equal or higher priority and cannot be displaced. Supported by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' in all three check messages.

Cluster autoscaler not active or too slow: if autoscaling were functioning, a new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node would have been provisioned within the ~144s window. The absence of any successful scheduling suggests autoscaling did not trigger or did not complete in time.

Concurrent eval runs or other workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are simultaneously holding VM slots, the pool could be transiently exhausted even if total capacity is nominally sufficient.

Because no preemption victims were found, the scheduler gave up and the pod remained unschedulable for 148 seconds before the eval runner surfaced the failure. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T14:57–15:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 126–148 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource type. The four remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling. Because no VM is ever provisioned, the eval probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling phase, and the check terminates with an Unschedulable error rather than returning any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 148s, zero evidence keys — all three checks in the remote-agents feature share the same infrastructure failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new pods.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource entirely (not registered or not labeled), so they are excluded by both the resource request and the pod's node affinity/selector, making the capacity problem structurally worse than a simple quota issue.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node drain, or node failure reduced the number of kata-peerpods-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking available vm-slot capacity below the level needed to schedule eval probes concurrently with production workloads.

[Possible] The pod's node affinity/selector is overly restrictive (e.g., targeting a specific node pool label) and no longer matches the nodes that have remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, creating a mismatch even if raw capacity exists elsewhere in the cluster.

[Less likely] A misconfiguration in the remote-agent pod spec (resource request quantity for kata.peerpods.io/vm) was recently changed to a value that exceeds per-node limits, making the pod unschedulable even on otherwise eligible nodes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the scheduler message would need a different explanation (e.g., a bug in the resource accounting plugin).

If re-running the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held lock or a race condition during concurrent probe runs) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the affinity/selector is confirmed correct, the problem is isolated to the 2 eligible nodes only and the affinity hypothesis is disproved.

If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, the resource exhaustion hypothesis is disproved and the cause may be a node-level plugin failure or misconfigured resource advertisement.

If the pod spec's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request quantity was recently changed to exceed per-node limits, that would shift the cause from capacity exhaustion to a misconfigured request, which would be disproved if the request quantity matches historical values.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all cluster nodes and warns when available slots fall below a configurable threshold (e.g., fewer than N slots remaining), providing early warning before pod scheduling fails.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes between 'pod scheduled but VM not ready' and 'pod never scheduled', enabling faster triage of scheduling vs. VM-provisioning failures in future incidents.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T15:00–15:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the runner never reached the state-polling step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. Every attempt to schedule a new remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" on the other 4. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). Because no pod could be scheduled, createAgent() in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905) never returned a live agent, and the state-polling logic that would produce orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence was never reached. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in all three check messages.

Preemption policy prevents eviction of lower-priority pods: the scheduler found no preemption victims on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning existing pods are equal or higher priority and cannot be displaced. Supported by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' in all three check messages.

Cluster autoscaler not active or too slow: if autoscaling were functioning, a new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable node would have been provisioned within the ~144s window. The absence of any successful scheduling suggests autoscaling did not trigger or did not complete in time.

Concurrent eval runs or other workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are simultaneously holding VM slots, the pool could be transiently exhausted even if total capacity is nominally sufficient.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected by any check, and no preemption path was available, causing each pod to remain unschedulable until the eval timed out.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-16T15:02:34Z–15:05:06Z), 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already at capacity, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because no preemption victims were found, the scheduler gave up and the pod remained unschedulable for 148 seconds before the eval runner surfaced the failure. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to the AURA observability eval for the remote-agents feature.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — the pod creation attempt is the first blocking operation and the point where scheduling fails
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: both VM-capable nodes are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks report the same scheduler message, confirming this is a cluster-wide capacity shortage at the time of the eval run.

SECONDARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or target a node label that has drifted, the effective schedulable pool is permanently limited to the 2 kata-capable nodes, making exhaustion more likely.

TERTIARY — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots: other tenant or system pods may have claimed all kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations before the eval pods were submitted, leaving no room even for short-lived eval agents.

LOWER — eval runner sequencing: remote-agent-create ran first (endedAt 15:00:06), remote-agent-state second (endedAt 15:02:34), and remote-agent-runtime third (endedAt 15:05:06). If create succeeded it would have held a VM slot during state and runtime checks; however, create also failed, so slot contention from the eval itself is unlikely to be the sole cause.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity in the production cluster to determine how many VM slots are allocated versus available on the 2 kata-capable nodes.
If VM slots are exhausted, identify which pods are holding them and whether any can be evicted, scaled down, or have their resource limits reduced to free capacity for eval and production workloads.

Review the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod template to confirm that restricting scheduling to 2 nodes is intentional and that those 2 nodes have sufficient VM slot headroom for concurrent eval and production use.

Consider adding more kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to the cluster or increasing the VM slot quota on existing nodes if the current pool is undersized for the expected concurrency of remote-agent workloads.
Add a Kubernetes node resource utilization alert for kata.peerpods.io/vm slots so that approaching exhaustion is detected before evals and production workloads are blocked.
After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agents eval checks to confirm they pass and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are collected.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is persistent (sustained exhaustion) or transient (momentary contention). A pass on re-run would indicate transient capacity pressure; a repeat fail confirms sustained exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Query kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated on all 6 nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly measures remaining VM slot capacity on each node. If both kata-capable nodes show 0 remaining slots, exhaustion is confirmed. If slots are available, the scheduler message may indicate a different admission or quota issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect remote-agent pod spec node affinity and selector rules
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4 non-kata nodes are excluded by design (correct) or by a label drift or misconfiguration (incorrect). If the affinity is correct, the fix is capacity; if incorrect, the fix is the pod spec or node labels.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks simultaneously and capture scheduler events
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether all three checks fail together under the same scheduler constraint, ruling out any check-specific issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check whether local-agent checks pass in the same run window
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If local-agent checks pass while remote-agent checks fail, the problem is isolated to the remote-agent node pool and kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, not a broader cluster or API outage.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were available and unallocated on both capable nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create check passed (pod scheduled successfully) in a concurrent or immediately subsequent run without any cluster changes, the failure would be transient contention rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 non-kata nodes were updated to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or the pod's node affinity was relaxed and scheduling still failed, the affinity misconfiguration hypothesis would be disproved.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed with the same scheduler message, the problem would extend beyond the remote-agent node pool and indicate a broader cluster issue rather than a remote-agent-specific capacity shortage.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and allocated counts across all cluster nodes and asserts that remaining capacity is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 1 free slot), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity is above a minimum count, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Add a scheduler-latency eval that measures the time from pod submission to pod Running state for a remote-agent pod and warns if it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), surfacing capacity pressure before full scheduling failures occur.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create on a reduced schedule (e.g., every 5 minutes) and alerts on two consecutive scheduling failures, enabling faster detection of sustained VM slot exhaustion.
